text:
ella: Heads-up — canary rollout we kicked off ~18:10 PST shows a ~32% token/sec drop on ctb hosts after the runtime merge 0b4f1c. Queueing delays and much smaller batch sizes than baseline. Should we halt? :eyes:
sam: I’m seeing a spike in memcpy wall time on the new kernel routing path. Kernel selection looks different for short prefixes — might be routing into an unoptimized memcpy-heavy kernel.
michael: perf-ci actually flagged a regression build earlier this morning but the presubmit was green for functional tests, so it slipped. Link: https://perf.ci/reports/3109876
perf-ci-bot: Performance regression detected on branch main. metric: tokens/sec. delta: -30% vs baseline (p95 latency +120ms). CI job: runtime-e2e/throughput-ctb.
justine: KV cache metrics from the affected hosts: hitrate dropped 0.72 -> 0.18 for popular models (gpt-like). That explains more cache misses + longer token processing.
ana: wait, whoops typo — ana: recommend we pause the rollout and run a targeted bisect. This is a rollout blocker.
ella: pausing rollout now. @dev-bot can you pause the canary rollout?
dev-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for cluster inference-canary-4. Action: hold.
sam: I pushed a quick flamegraph capture on one of the canary instances — main hot path shows heavy time in kernel_router::choose_kernel() then memcpy path in kernel_B. Snippet: ```flamegraph: kernel_router::choose_kernel -> kernel_B::memcopy 48%```
michael: good call. I’ll start a local bisect: `git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad` then mark bad at 0b4f1c and good at a7b2f90. Running microbench to validate.
justine: also capture `kvcache.metrics` and `batcher.window_size` traces. The batcher is creating 3-4 token batches frequently (should be 12-16).
zach: I suspect the router heuristic that picks kernel by seq-len histogram changed behavior because we now include new prefetch weight. Could cause smaller batch coalescing.
sam: quick local repro: checkout 0b4f1c -> run bench_ctb.sh -> tokens/sec 420k. Checkout good a7b2f90 -> tokens/sec 610k. So bisect points at that merge.
michael: confirm. Bisect shows first bad commit is 0b4f1c (scheduler: kernel routing heuristics + prefetch tuning).
ana: ana: please open a revert PR and add a hold in the rollout until we patch kernel routing to respect batcher hints.
ana: opened PR #4128 to revert 0b4f1c and added a rollback changelog. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128
ella: thanks. Meanwhile, sam can you add an experiment that forces `kernel_selector=legacy` on canary so we can validate patch vs revert?
sam: yes, running a canary with `KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy` now. If tokens/sec recovers we have a clear fingerprint.
perf-ci-bot: New perf job queued: runtime/throughput-legacy-kernel.
justine: dashboard note — I added a temporary alert on `batch_size.mean < 6` and `kvcache.hitrate < 0.4` to surface this earlier.
zach: also adding structured logging around `choose_kernel()` with `selected_kernel` and `reason_code` so we can see why it picked kernel_B for short prefixes. Will ship short patch to canary.
michael: running flamegraphs + `perf record` on the legacy vs new kernel selection, will attach artifacts.
ella: update: revert PR merged to canary branch and rollout paused. Preliminary metrics: tokens/sec back to ~610k on reverted hosts, queueing delays normalized, batch sizes resumed to 12-14.
ana: follow-ups: (1) harden kernel selector tests in CI with a micro-benchmark (2) add regression perf job for ctb throughput (3) add kvcache smoke in post-deploy checks.
ella: agree. I'll file a tracking ticket and assign owners. Thanks everyone for quick bisect+revert. :tada:
